messages:
alex.m: Heads-up — I'm about to land a small TF change that flips our inference deployment from RollingUpdate to a two-phase StatefulSet rollout for the gpu-worker sts. Reason: PVC attach race when scaling from 0 -> N during canary.

maya: curious — can you sketch the two-phase plan? Is this the same partitioned update pattern we've used elsewhere?

alex.m: yep similar. Plan is: 1) create new sts with minReplicas=1 and partitioned updates for steady-state, 2) pre-create PVCs with consistent names in TF, 3) use a startup probe wait in the pod that checks for the secret+kms key binding to exist, then unpause rollout. Should avoid attach races.

chris: quick Q — where will the precreated PVCs live? do we namespace them per-cluster? Terraform wants to create pvcs with for_each which might collide if someone runs it twice.

alex.m: PVCs live in the same k8s namespace (inference-prod). TF will use a lifecycle create_before_destroy and name prefix = var.cluster_suffix to reduce collisions. I'll add a guard so apply fails if a PVC with same name already exists but not managed by TF.

maya: can you paste the startup probe snippet you're planning? want to check timeout behavior for large models.

alex.m: sure — planning something like: ```yaml
startupProbe:
  exec:
    command: ["/bin/sh","-c","/usr/local/bin/wait-for-secret.sh kms://projects/myproj/keys/inference-key && curl -f http://localhost:8080/health || exit 1"]
  failureThreshold: 60
  periodSeconds: 10
```
That gives ~10 minutes for KMS propagation in worst-case.

chris: 10 minutes is long but ok for canary. Does wait-for-secret.sh fallback if secret isn't present? We don't want pods stuck forever during ctrl-plane issues.

alex.m: it will exit nonzero after timeout — that's handled by k8s (pod fails, restart). I added a Circuit Breaker in console that will prevent us from ramping beyond 2 replicas until health is stable.

infra-bot: @alex.m created PR #4123: tf/sts-precreate-pvcs + startup-probe (reviewers: maya, chris) :eyes:

maya: marked for review. One thing: for the StatefulSet updateStrategy we should set `rollingUpdate.partition` to the current ordinal of the live instance during the canary switch, not hardcode. Otherwise we might accidentally replace the canary pod.

alex.m: good call — will wire in an env from the rollout job that sets the partition value dynamically. PR will add a small controller job that annotates the sts with the partition before patch.

chris: also flagging a terraform-state concern: we create PVCs + sts in same apply. If the STS controller sees volumes before TF finishes attachments, could still race. Thinking we separate into two applies: 1) create PVCs 2) apply sts. Is that doable in CI?

alex.m: yep I'll split the pipeline. CI job 1 precreates PVCs via `terraform apply -target=module.pvcs`, job 2 runs the rest after a short verify. I'll add a manual approval gate for production run.

maya: what about rollback? If sts fails to bring up because secret KMS mapping is wrong, how do we quickly revert?

alex.m: we'll keep old sts around for 10m using partitioned update (old pods won't be killed until new are ready). For quick revert we have a runbook: set annotation rollout=cancel which the rollout job watches and restores partition=0 -> patches back. I'll add the runbook to the PR description.

sre-oncall: ping: can we add an alert if >3 restarts in 5m for pods in inference-prod/gpu-worker? If the startupProbe is too aggressive we'll want early signal.

chris: agreed. I'll add a prometheus rule: pod:container_restart_count:rate5m > 3 -> pager to oncall. Also monitor kube_pod_container_status_waiting_reason{reason=\"AttachVolume\"} spikes.

alex.m: thanks — I'll update PR and split the CI steps, include the runbook and add the prometheus alert links. tagging @maya @chris for final review. :+1:
